observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The male and female instructors present information through a series of spoken segments while cutting to B-roll footage of dancers in country venues. They break down definitions, rhythms, and styles of various country dances in an enthusiastic and informative manner.

lesson_structure.note: Anthony and Rose introduce themselves and the video topic
Explanation and overview of Two Step
Explanation and overview of Country Swing
Explanation and overview of Country Line Dance
Explanation and overview of West Coast Swing

metaphors: travels around the room like a race track
get on that train right now

steps_taught.name: Two Step
steps_taught.description: Progressive dance with two quick steps and two slow steps.

steps_taught.name: Country Swing
steps_taught.description: Spot dance with circular turns, dips, and lifts.

steps_taught.name: Country Line Dance
steps_taught.description: Choreographed steps danced in a line without a partner.

steps_taught.name: West Coast Swing
steps_taught.description: Spot dance danced in a slot with smooth styling.

what_works: Clear verbal definitions contrasting each dance style
Visual examples of dancers in country bars
what_hinders: Lacks step-by-step physical breakdown of footwork in the tutorial segment

quotes.text: Two Step is the country dance.
First of all, Two Step is a progressive dance.
So we count it quick, quick, slow, slow.
Country Swing is growing so amazingly fast.
Country Line Dance, because that's what people picture in their mind.

evidence_segments.observation: Two instructors standing side by side in a living room setting, talking to the camera with hand gestures.

extraction.distinctive_method: Explaining multiple distinct country dance styles (Two Step, Country Swing, Line Dance, West Coast Swing) in a single introductory video overview using B-roll clip illustrations.
